biography.ja:
ウィーンで生まれ、同時代のベートーヴェンを深く敬愛したが、生前に二人が親しく交流することはなかったとされる。宮廷礼拝堂の少年合唱団を経て一時教師を務めたが、多くは特定の職に就かず、友人たちが自宅に集って彼の新作を演奏する私的な集まり「シューベルティアーデ」を主な発表の場とした。
歌曲だけで600曲以上を書くなど驚異的な多作家だったが、生前に広く名声を得ることはなく、31歳で病のため早世した。
biography.en:
Born in Vienna, he deeply admired his contemporary Beethoven, though the two are not thought to have had any close acquaintance during their lifetimes. After time as a boy in the imperial court chapel choir and briefly working as a schoolteacher, he held no fixed post for most of his life, relying instead on private gatherings at friends' homes — the so-called Schubertiades — where his newest works were performed.
He was astonishingly prolific, writing more than six hundred songs alone, but achieved little wide recognition in his lifetime and died of illness at thirty-one.

style.ja: 歌曲では、ピアノ伴奏を単なる添え物にとどめず、歌詞の心理状態や情景を音型そのもので描写する手法を確立した。糸車の回転を表す反復音型や、旅の終わりに響くハーディ・ガーディの単調な響きなど、伴奏が詩の内容と直接結びついている。複数の歌曲を一つの物語としてまとめる「連作歌曲」という形式も確立した。器楽曲でも歌うような旋律を貫き、急がず伸びやかに主題を繰り返し変奏していく、ゆったりとした構成を好んだ。
style.en: In his songs he established a technique in which the piano is no mere accompaniment but paints the psychological state or scene of the text directly in its figuration — a repeating pattern for a spinning wheel, or the drone of a hurdy-gurdy at the end of a long journey. He also established the song cycle, binding a sequence of songs into a single narrative. His instrumental music keeps the same songful lyricism, favouring a leisurely structure that repeats and varies its material without symphonic urgency.

impact.ja: 歌曲を家庭内の娯楽的な音楽から、交響曲やオペラに匹敵する重みを持つ芸術形式へと引き上げ、ドイツ・リートという分野そのものを確立した。彼が切り拓いた連作歌曲の形式は、のちにシューマンが自身の歌曲集で受け継いでいる。死後に埋もれていた大規模な器楽曲の草稿は、シューマンによって発見されて世に知らされ、メンデルスゾーンの指揮によって初演されるなど、後続の作曲家たちの手で再評価が進んだ。
impact.en: He raised the song from domestic entertainment into an art form carrying as much weight as the symphony or opera, founding the German Lied as a field in its own right. The song-cycle form he pioneered was carried forward by Schumann in his own song cycles. Manuscripts of his large-scale instrumental works, buried and unknown after his death, were found and brought to light by Schumann and had their premiere under Mendelssohn's baton — his reputation rebuilt, piece by piece, through the efforts of the composers who came after him.

story.ja: 1827年のベートーヴェンの葬儀では松明を掲げる係の一人を務めた。翌年みずからが世を去った際、彼自身の希望によりベートーヴェンの墓のすぐそばに葬られている。
story.en: At Beethoven's funeral in 1827 he was one of the torchbearers. When he himself died the following year, he was buried, at his own request, right beside Beethoven's grave.
